messages:
Olivia Chen: quick follow-up from the RFC thread — proposing we prune the centralized debt-ledger table and introduce an Ownership Annotation service that stores lightweight ownership pointers per-tenant. goal: reduce hotpath contention, simplify ownership changes, and make per-tenant paydown ops safer. sketch of proposal:
- writes: keep writing to ledger for now, also write an annotation pointer to new service (dual-write).
- reads: read annotation first; fall back to ledger until backfill completes.
- migration: background backfill moves authoritative pointers to annotation service, then flip the read path and stop writes to ledger.
- safety: canary by tenant cohort, circuit-breaker if lag > X, read-fallback for N days.
Thoughts on tradeoffs (consistency, cost, rollback)?

Frank Rivera: short: +1 for ownership map approach. main tradeoff is consistency during coexistence. are we ok with eventual consistency for ownership changes? what SLA do we need for ownership reads?

Jia Patel: my worry is read-path latency for the hotpath (generation requests). an extra network hop could add 3-6ms p50; need numbers. can we colocate annotation caches with the serving plane?

Samir Gupta: prefer storing only a pointer (ownership_id + version) in annotation service, not full history. that keeps record small and cheap. also suggest TTL for old pointers and a retention policy.

Olivia Chen: exactly — annotation = (tenant_id -> owner_id, owner_version, source_ts). no history in the hot read path. history lives in ledger archival store. for consistency: dual-write but treat annotation as single source-of-truth after backfill completes. rollback plan below.

Frank Rivera: rollout questions: how do we handle concurrent ownership flips? e.g., transfer that happens during backfill. we need a compare-and-swap GUID on owner_version. otherwise races will clobber.

Olivia Chen: agreed. annotation write API will be conditional on owner_version (CAS). sequence: on transfer start, bump tentative_version, write to annotation with CAS, then confirm after acceptance. if CAS fails, caller retries. adds complexity but safer.

Jia Patel: can we measure the p50 penalty of an annotation read when colocated vs remote? I can run perf spike against staging if we have an endpoint.

Olivia Chen: yes please, @Jia. staging endpoint will be: https://staging-annotator.internal/lookup?tenant={id} — expect small JSON. planning a perf spike Wednesday.

Samir Gupta: migration commands I used in previous prune: simple backfill runner + dry-run mode. propose we expose the same pattern:
```
# dry-run for tenant cohort alpha
./bin/debt_backfill --cohort=alpha --batch=500 --dry-run
# real run
./bin/debt_backfill --cohort=alpha --batch=500
```
Keep backfill idempotent and resumable.

Olivia Chen: rollback and safety plan (short):
1) start with dry-run, validate pointer correctness for cohort.
2) enable dual-write for cohort, monitor replication lag and error rate.
3) run backfill until 99.9% of reads resolve to annotation (monitor tail).
4) flip reads to annotation for cohort; keep ledger writes for extra 24-72h.
5) if error/latency/regression -> flip reads back to ledger, resume dual-write until fixed.
All flips are feature-flagged and reversible.

Frank Rivera: monitoring checklist: replication lag metric, CAS failure rate, p50/p99 read latency, error rate in generation pipeline, number of read fallbacks. also cost delta (RPS * annotation read cost).

debt-bot: scheduled deployment: staging/annotator v0.1 -> Wed 09:00 UTC (2611112600). CI passed: unit/integ.

Jia Patel: acked. I'll run perf spike after deploy and drop numbers here. expecting to validate colocated vs remote.

Samir Gupta: I'll draft the migration runbook and the CAS semantics doc. include rollback commands and how to force-read-legacy for debugging.

Olivia Chen: great. next steps: @Jia perf spike Wed, @Samir runbook draft by EOD Thu, I'll prepare feature flags and cohort list. if anyone objects to the plan, speak now. otherwise I'll open the PR for the pseudo-CAS API and annotation schema. :thumbsup:
